title: A Story of Change
dateline: Village Gunj, Yavatmal, Maharashtra · Rajkumar Kishan Gore, Organic Cotton Farmer · 3.64 Hectares

image.alt: Rajkumar Kishan Gore in his cotton field

children.text: The soil in village Gunj used to smell like the market: sharp, chemical, nothing like earth. Rajkumar Kishan Gore worked that soil for years before he learned there was another way.

Rajkumar farms 3.64 hectares of cotton in village Gunj. Like most families in the region, farming isn't just his livelihood, it's the foundation everything else in his household is built on: his children's schooling, his family's food security, his standing in the community.

For years, he farmed the way everyone around him did, buying chemical fertiliser and pesticide from the market, season after season. The inputs alone cost him ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 an acre. His soil grew tired under the chemical load. His health suffered from years of handling pesticide. And despite the rising costs, his yields kept slipping, not climbing.

TCMCF arrived in village Gunj with a simple idea: make it yourself. Rajkumar joined the village's newly formed Organic Producer Group and, through TCMCF's training, learned to turn five leaves, cow dung, and soybean into everything his fields needed: five-leaf extract, Amrutpani, and a soybean-based nutrient tonic, all produced on his own land, at a fraction of the cost of what he used to buy.

content.quote: Chemical pesticides were destroying my soil and my health. Today, I make my own inputs, for a fraction of the cost. Our costs have come down. Our production has gone up.

children.text: The difference showed fast. Input costs that once ran ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 an acre fell to just ₹200 to ₹300, a reduction of roughly 96%. His cotton yield climbed 25 to 30%, the kind of number that changes how a family plans its year, not just its season.

items.label: Reduction in input cost per acre

children.text: Rajkumar didn't keep what he'd learned to himself. He started walking his neighbours through the same process, farm by farm, field by field. What began as one man's shift away from chemical inputs is slowly becoming how the whole village farms, easing input costs, restoring soil health, and building income security for an entire community, not just one household.

closing: Rajkumar’s story is the model. 27,000 more farmers are walking the same path. Support this work at changemakers.org.in.
